items.text: The Jordanian military reports that air defenses have intercepted 8 out of 10 projectiles fired by Iran against the country in Aqaba near the Israeli border, with two missiles landing in remote areas. ((ABC News)) ((CBC)) ((Ynetnews))
The General Staff of the Kuwait Army reports that Kuwait's military and air defenses have been actively intercepting "hostile drones" from Iran. ((Arab Times Kuwait)) ((The Times Kuwait))
The United States military launches Tomahawk missiles strikes on Iran's Larak Island. ((AFP via Al Arabiya))
The U.S. Central Command launches a new round of strikes against Iran, marking the 12th consecutive day of attacks. ((AP)) ((Middle East Eye))

Financial Times reports that the tanker Kavomalaes, belonging to Greek shipowner George Prokopiou, was "highly likely" to have been captured in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran two days earlier. ((Forbes))

Seven oil tankers departing Saudi Arabia's port of Yanbu change course away from the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb after the Houthis announced a blockade on Saudi Arabian ports. ((The Washington Post)) ((Reuters))
UNICEF reports that six people, including two children, have been killed and 30 people including children have been injured in a drone strike on a market in Al-Rahad, North Kordofan, Sudan. ((AA))

A Chadian official reports that a drone attack from Sudanese territory has attacked positions in Chad, injuring civilians and destroying vehicles and several shops. The attack is the fifth in recent months, following an incursion by Rapid Support Forces last January. ((Sudan Tribune))
Five soldiers are killed and six civilians are injured in a mass shooting by ten unknown gunmen at a security checkpoint in Narathiwat province, Thailand. ((Al Jazeera))
A 35-year-old head constable is shot and killed in a militant attack in Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir, India. The Resistance Front claims responsibility. ((NDTV))

Oil prices, including Brent Crude and West Texas Intermediate, rise to over US$95 and $86 per barrel, respectively, and the United States average gasoline price rises to $4.06 per gallon, amidst the ongoing conflict. ((CNBC)) ((NBC News))
A Robinson R44 helicopter crashes in Sincan, Ankara, Turkey, killing the pilot and injuring the co-pilot. ((Turkiye Today))

In the United States, West Virginia governor Patrick Morrisey declares a state of emergency and announces that 100 National Guard troops have been deployed after flash floods caused by torrential rains were reported across the state, including the northern part. ((AP)) ((The Independent))
The death toll from the ongoing measles outbreak in Bangladesh exceeds past 800. ((The Business Standard)) ((Dhaka Tribune))
African CDC director Jean Kaseya reports that the death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached past 1,000. ((AP))
The number of reported cyclosporiasis cases in the U.S. state of Michigan exceeds 7,000. ((WDIV))

Revolution Medicines announces that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has accepted for review the company's New Drug Application (NDA) for the RAS inhibitor drug daraxonrasib as a treatment for metastatic pancreatic cancer. ((The Manila Times)) ((MarketWatch))

Saudi Arabia and the United States sign a civil nuclear cooperation agreement allowing Saudi Arabia to use U.S. reactor technology, enrich uranium, and reprocess nuclear waste. The pact excludes the IAEA Additional Protocol and proceeds to U.S. congressional review. ((AFP via France 24)) ((Reuters))

The federal trial against Hadi Matar, the man who attempted to kill author Salman Rushdie in August 2022 in New York, United States, opens. If he is convicted, Matar faces a sentence of life in prison. He is already serving a 25-year state prison sentence in New York. ((AP)) ((The Guardian))

Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi is released after police detained him outside prime minister Narendra Modi's residence yesterday during protests demanding education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and changes to the examination system. ((AFP via France 24))
The United States military launches Tomahawk missile strikes on Iran's Larak Island. ((AFP via Al Arabiya))

The Israel Defense Forces and Shin Bet announces that they have killed three Hamas militants in the northern Gaza Strip, including one in the Hamas military wing that took part in the October 7 attacks on Israel. ((The Jerusalem Post)) ((Cleveland Jewish News))
Seven people are killed after a truck collided with a medical transport van in Pernambuco, Brazil. ((Xinhua))
The number of reported cyclosporiasis cases in the U.S. state of Michigan exceeds 7,000. ((Reuters)) ((WDIV))

The fire department of Tokyo, Japan, reports 453 heat-related hospitalizations, its highest daily total since records began in 2010, as a severe heat wave kills one person and leaves four critically ill. The country's Fire and Disaster Management Agency reports at least 14 heat-related deaths nationwide over the previous week. ((AFP via Malay Mail))
Unknown gunmen open fire at a police station in Canindeyú Department, Paraguay, killing three officers and wounding another. ((Abc.com))

Sixteen civilians, most of whom gold miners, are killed during a village attack suspected to have been perpetrated by ADF forces in Mandeite locality, Mambasa, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. ((AA))
Seven people are killed after a truck collides with a medical transport van in Pernambuco, Brazil. ((Xinhua))
The death toll from the ongoing measles outbreak in Bangladesh exceeds 800. ((The Business Standard)) ((Dhaka Tribune))

The European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope reports evidence of a possible exomoon-like object orbiting the brown dwarf CD-35 2722 B in the CD-35 2722 system, in a study published in the Nature journal. ((Space.com)) ((Phys.org)) ((Nature))

Pope Leo XIV consecrates Fr. Joseph Chang Yanfeng as the bishop of Chifeng in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China under the 2018 provisional framework, which cedes authority over its bishops to the Chinese government. ((Holy See)) ((Vatican News))
